name: Mxwlsoft Post Row Colors – Background Highlighter for Admin
author: mxwlsoft

sections.description:
Do you find it hard to quickly locate specific content in a long list of posts or pages? Mxwlsoft Post Row Colors lets you assign a custom background color to each post or page row in the WordPress admin list table. This helps you visually organize, distinguish, and highlight content.

Key features:

  • Color-coded rows – Set a different background color for each post/page row. Instantly spot what matters.
  • 10 built-in colors – Choose from soft red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, light gray, or white.
  • Easy to use:
    • In the post editor, use the “Background Color” panel in the sidebar.
    • In the list table, use Quick Edit to change the color inline.
    • Use Bulk Edit to apply the same color to multiple posts at once.
  • No configuration – Activate and it works immediately. No settings page needed.

Use cases:

  • Mark important, pending, or featured posts.
  • Visually group content by category, author, or status (e.g., green = published, yellow = needs update, red = needs review).
  • Quickly spot specific entries in personal blogs or business websites.
sections.installation:
1. From your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Mxwlsoft Post Row Colors”, or upload the plugin folder.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Posts or Pages. You will see a new “Background Color” column in the list table.
  4. Click Quick Edit on any post, or edit the post directly, to choose a color.
sections.faq:
How do I set a background color for a post?

Two ways:
– Edit screen: Open the post editor. On the right sidebar, find the “Background Color” panel, pick a color, and save.
– Quick Edit: In the post list table, hover over a post title, click Quick Edit, choose a color from the field, then click Update.

Can I set the same color for multiple posts at once?

Yes. Select several posts, then choose Bulk Edit. In the bulk edit panel, pick a color and click Update.

How do I remove a color?

In the color picker, clear the color value (delete all characters) and save. The row will return to the default white background.

Which post types are supported?

By default, Posts and Pages are supported.

Will the colors affect my website’s front end?

No. This plugin works only in the WordPress admin area. It does not change anything on the public side of your site.
